CITY OF ALHAMBRA PLANNING COMMISSION
  ACTION MINUTES

  Regular Meeting
  March 15, 2021

A.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER:  7:01 P.M. via video conference and teleconference

B.  ROLL CALL:
  Present:  Messina, Olson, Sahu, Tang, Tsujii, Wang, E. Garcia, Gardea,

  Absent:  Moreno Garcia

  Vice President E. Garcia arrived at 7:03 PM

  Staff Present: Vanessa Reynoso, Deputy Director, Paul Lam, Principal Planner, Scott
  Quyle, Associate Planner, and Erica Vega, Deputy City Attorney

C.  FLAG SALUTE:  Led by President Gardea

D.  CONSENT AGENDA:

  ITEM 1:  MINUTES – FEBRUARY 16, 2021
  Recommended Action: Approve as submitted.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Consent Calendar Item 1.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Olson, Seconded by Commissioner Sahu
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 7-0
  Ayes:  Messina, Olson, Sahu, Tang, Tsujii, Wang, Gardea
  Noes:  None
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  Moreno Garcia, E. Garcia

 E.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  ITEM 2:  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT PD-20-18 AND CONDITIONAL
  USE PERMIT CUP-21-10
  • 601 West Valley Boulevard
  • Request: This is an application for a Planned Development Permit and
  Conditional Use Permit to demolish an existing 1,596 square foot
  convenience store to construct a new 2,882 square foot convenience
  store on an approximate land area of 16,522 square feet located at 601
  West Valley Boulevard (APN 5350-007-018) located in the VSP-RC
  (Valley Specific Plan - Retail Commercial) zone. The existing four (4)
  gas pump canopy is not being altered.
  • Recommended Action: Pending public testimony, adopt Resolution
  No. 21-08, approving Planned Development Permit PD-20-18 and
  Conditional Use Permit CUP-21-10, subject to the Conditions of
  Approval.
  • Associate Planner Scott Quyle provided staff presentation.
  • Public Comments: There were none.
  • Commissioner Comments:
  Several Commissioners had concerns with the existing entrance on 6th
  Street and the back-up width from Parking Space Number 10 to the
  proposed building.
  Commissioner Messina had concerns with the proposed building
  being constructed on the rear property line along the back alley which
  the Fire Department utilizes.
  Commissioner Sahu had questions with regard to what retail products
  would be sold and the on-site automotive circulation.
  Commissioner Tsujii had a question regarding the minimum distance
  an entrance must be from an intersection.
  President Gardea had questions regarding the landscaping along the
  western property line.
  Commissioner Tang had questions regarding the proposed ADA
  upgrades.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Planned Development Permit PD-20-18 and
  Conditional Use Permit CUP-21-10 with two added conditions of approval
  to resolve concerns with parking space number 10 and to consider
  reconfiguration of the 6th Street entrance/exit without closing it, and to
  amend Condition PL15 to say South 6th Street.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu. Seconded by Commissioner Olson.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 7-1
  Ayes:  Olson, Sahu, Tang, Tsujii, Wang, E. Garcia, Gardea
  Noes:  Messina
  2
  03/15/2021
   Abstain:  None
  Absent:  Moreno Garcia

ITEM 3:  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CUP-20-04 AND LOT MERGER
  LOTM-2021-01
  • 1318 & 1322 Alhambra Road
  • Request: This is a request for a Conditional Use Permit and a Lot
  Merger to allow a meditation center to occupy an existing 5,000 square
  foot building that was previously a market. Property improvements are
  proposed to bring the property into conformance with the Zoning and
  General Plan regulations on an approximate land area of 16,500 square
  feet located in the R-2 (Limited Multiple Family Residential) zone.
  • Recommended Action: Pending public testimony, adopt Resolution
  No. 21-07, approving Conditional Use Permit CUP-20-04 and Lot
  Merger LOTM-2021-01, subject to the Conditions of Approval.
  • Associate Planner Scott Quyle provided staff presentation.
  • Public Comments: There were a total of 36 public comments and one
  (1) request to speak. However, the person who requested to speak was
  not present. Approximately half of the letters were in support of the
  project while the other half was opposed it. Those opposed raised
  concerns regarding the use’s holding of large events, noise,
  incompatibility with residential neighborhood and traffic. Those who
  were in support voiced excitement for the use and issued statements
  stating that traffic and noise would not be an issue.
  • Commissioner Comments:
  Several Commissioners had concerns with onsite parking, the
  maximum occupancy of the building and the potential for large events,
  and that the property would be better suited for residential purposes.
  Commissioner Olson had questions regarding the overall building
  capacity and how does staff verify conditions are being met, the hours
  of operations, and a 6-month review.
  Vice President E. Garcia had questions regarding the planter’s height,
  the greenbelt, and the building’s color.
  Commissioner Tsujii had question regarding parking overflow plan,
  and the need for restricting access to the entrance/exit to the north.
  Commissioner Wang had questions regarding the intended audience.
  Commissioner Sahu had questions regarding the need for a
  multipurpose room.

  3
  03/15/2021
   MOTION:
  •  Moved to deny Conditional Use Permit CUP-20-04 and Lot Merger
  LOTM-2021-01 and have staff return with a Resolution of Denial.
  •  Moved by Vice President E. Garcia. Seconded by Commissioner Messina.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 7-1

  Ayes:  Messina, Olson, Sahu, Tang, Wang, E. Garcia, Gardea
  Noes:  Tsujii,
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  Moreno Garcia

F.  DIRECTOR’S REPORT:

  •  There were none

G.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

  •  There were none.

H.  COMMISSION ORALS:

  •  Commissioner Tang expressed his desire for Staff to consider adopting an ADU
  ordinance similar to that of San Gabriel which limits ADUs to one (1) story and 1,000
  square feet. Discussion ensued regarding this matter. Vice President E. Garcia and
  Commissioner Sahu inquired about a Planning Commission subcommittee to discuss
  ADU matters.

  •  President Gardea stated that here have been changes made at the State level which
  have updated the ADU laws. President Gardea also inquired whether the direction for
  ADUs would be a Council direction.
